title: Indoor Condition Observation Series
researchQuestion: How closely do brief room-comfort observations align with ordinary temperature and relative-humidity readings over seven consecutive days?
summary: This remote observation series compares a participant's simple description of one indoor environment with readings from an ordinary household thermo-hygrometer. The protocol is concerned with consistency of observation, not health, diagnosis, or building inspection.
commitment: Three brief observations daily for seven days
eligibility: Regular access to the same ordinary indoor room for seven consecutive days.
Able to make three observations during a consistent morning, afternoon, and evening window.
A household temperature and relative-humidity display is useful but not required.
exclusions: No workplace, clinical, secure, or otherwise sensitive location may be used.
No health symptoms, resident identities, photographs, addresses, or precise location information are requested.
participantActivities: Choose one ordinary indoor room and retain the same observation position for the full series.
At each interval, record a neutral comfort category, whether a window or exterior door was recently open, and available temperature or relative-humidity readings.
Complete one short end-of-series check describing schedule consistency and any ordinary interruption to the observation sequence.

protocolSteps.title: Select
protocolSteps.description: Choose one non-sensitive indoor observation point that can remain consistent for seven days.

protocolSteps.title: Observe
protocolSteps.description: Make one morning, afternoon, and evening observation within stable daily windows.

protocolSteps.title: Record
protocolSteps.description: Use fixed response categories and note instrument readings only when a display is available.

protocolSteps.title: Review
protocolSteps.description: Check the seven-day log for missed intervals and ordinary environmental changes.

dataRequested: Broad indoor climate description selected from fixed categories.
Availability and general type of a temperature or relative-humidity display.
Daily availability windows and confirmation of the seven-day commitment.
Fixed-category observations of room comfort and recent ventilation.
dataNotRequested: Name, email address, telephone number, or date of birth.
Street address, coordinates, IP-derived location, photographs, or recordings.
Medical information, symptoms, diagnoses, or information about other occupants.
samplePrompts: At this interval, did the room feel cooler than expected, neutral, or warmer than expected?
Was a window or exterior door open during the preceding 30 minutes?
Was the observation made within the assigned time window?
methodNotes: The same response categories are used throughout the series so that changes in wording do not become changes in the observation scale.
Instrument readings are treated as contextual observations. Consumer displays are not assumed to be calibrated laboratory instruments.
A missed interval remains a missed interval; participants are not asked to reconstruct readings from memory.
limitations: Room selection, instrument placement, and household equipment vary between participants.
Self-reported comfort is an ordinal observation and is not interpreted as a medical or indoor-air-quality assessment.
The series is designed to describe observation consistency and cannot establish the cause of a particular reading.
